annotations.text:
VIGIL — a dead man's trigger

Warm paper, ink, and one ember. Serif for what a person wrote; sans for the machinery. Nothing is ever red — red means error, and none of this is an error.

Static mockups at 390×844. Tokens match apps/mobile/src/theme/tokens.ts exactly.

The flame is the entire status display — readable across a room without reading a word. Steady = all is well. Dimming = we've missed you. Slow pulse = we're trying to reach you. It never flashes and never turns red: the app must not be able to frighten someone who is simply on holiday.
Check-in is press-and-hold, not tap. It can't be done by a pocket, takes ~1.4s, and ends on a haptic full stop — a small ritual rather than a notification to dismiss.
The dated forecast is never behind a 'details' tap. Hollow marks = only you hear from us. Filled ember = another human is contacted. At a glance you can see the exact day this stops being private.

This sentence is generated from the real grant by describeCustody() in @vigil/crypto — not written by marketing. If the cryptography changes, the copy changes with it. 'On our own, we are one piece short' is a structural claim the test suite pins.

Deliberately not the app: no nav, no branding, no product. Someone bereaved is opening a link from a service they've never heard of. It should feel like being handed an envelope, and be in no hurry at all — hence 'Not today' as a first-class action.
